_what_this_is: Phase 3 acceptance, measured against the urds-agent Windows Service on an elevated host. One service lifetime per arm, so each arm runs against a decoy field the agent seeded itself. The criterion was: a third-party encryptor suspended within 20 files and under 2 s, with an ffmpeg transcode, a 7-Zip archive and a git clone running to completion untouched. One attack arm is suspended and misses the file bound; the other is not suspended at all. Recorded as failed rather than restated into something that passed.

criterion.attack: third-party encryptor suspended within 20 files and under 2 s
criterion.benign: ffmpeg transcode, 7-Zip archive and git clone complete untouched

corpus.why_this_size: The first attempt used 40 documents of 6 KB. Both arms finished that in under a second - 7-Zip archived it and exited before its own audit record arrived, at 980 ms - so FEBR was 40 of 40 whether the agent responded in 1.2 s or never responded at all. A corpus that is gone before the clock starts cannot measure a response time either way. The criterion is unchanged; the corpus is now large enough to answer it.

attack_arms.arm: A1 7z a -p -sdel over the whole directory (single process)
attack_arms.verdict: FAIL - 499 of 500 documents destroyed, nothing suspended
attack_arms.why_it_was_missed: Both halves of the system miss it, for reasons already documented separately. (1) Its output is a password-protected .7z at 8.0 bits/byte, and the detector adjudicates it benign_compressed - 'entropy 8.0 explained by a 7z header (this format has no structural validator)'. That is the Section 1.3 separability result: the project has structural validators for 6 of 17 formats and 7z is not one of them, so a legitimate archive and ciphertext under a 7z header are the same bytes. (2) 7-Zip's -sdel unlinks the originals only *after* the archive completes, so all 520 deletions land in the process's final moments and their audit records arrive about a second later, by which time 7z.exe has exited. The agent names it correctly - 'canary deleted: !_urds_canary_01.docx by pid 14120 (7z.exe)' - and the response guard reports that the PID no longer exists.

attack_arms.arm: A2 openssl enc -aes-256-cbc (one process per file)
attack_arms.verdict: PARTIAL - suspended at 1.972 s, inside the 2 s bound, having lost 37 of 500 documents. The file bound of 20 is missed.
attack_arms.how_it_was_caught: Not by the process that wrote the ciphertext. Each openssl lives about 65 ms against roughly 1000 ms of audit delivery lag, so every one of them was long gone before it could be named. What was caught is the loop driver, which unlinks each original - a long-lived process, named through the DELETE access right, on a decoy it removed. Ten of the twenty decoys were still on disk when it was suspended.

benign_arms.not_run: ffmpeg is not installed on this host. The arm is named in the brief and is reported as not run rather than substituted with a different tool.

benign_verdict: PASS on the three arms that ran, and unlike the first attempt this pass carries weight: the same build, in the same session, suspended arm A2 on a certain attribution. A clean sheet is evidence of specificity only when the detector was capable of acting. ffmpeg was not run - it is not installed on this host - and is reported as not run rather than substituted.

what_changed_since_the_first_attempt.dispatch_lanes: The watchdog thread now appends and returns; four path-sharded lanes do the work. Dropped events went from 175 to 0.
what_changed_since_the_first_attempt.attribution_window: 750 ms to 3000 ms, calibrated to a new measurement (reports/attribution_delivery_lag.json) showing delivery bounded at ~1010 ms and independent of write rate. 750 ms was below the delivery floor of the mechanism it reads: under a burst it matched 0 of 120 records.
what_changed_since_the_first_attempt.no_blocking_wait: The 250 ms blocking grace is off the detection path entirely. Events that cannot yet name a writer are parked and re-asked every 25 ms, so a lane is never held and the response fires the moment the record lands.
what_changed_since_the_first_attempt.delete_is_audited: DELETE was added to the SACL and to the parsed access mask. This is what makes arm A2 catchable at all: the writer is ephemeral and the deleter is not.
what_changed_since_the_first_attempt.a_deleted_decoy_is_a_hit: Deletions used to be skipped by the canary check on the grounds that a file that is gone cannot be hash-compared. An attack that archives and unlinks therefore walked through the whole decoy field without setting anything off.

root_cause_of_the_remaining_failure.summary: Audit delivery lag sets a floor on time-to-suspend, and therefore on FEBR. Nothing in the agent can go below it.
root_cause_of_the_remaining_failure.rule: FEBR >= delivery_lag * the attacker's write rate
root_cause_of_the_remaining_failure.worked: Arm A2 writes about 19 files/s, so at least 19 files are lost before any response is physically possible. 37 were lost.
root_cause_of_the_remaining_failure.the_rest_of_the_gap_is_queueing_and_is_n: 37 is roughly twice the 19 the delivery lag alone accounts for. The remainder is the agent's own queue: per-arm max_lag_ms reads 11-13 s, which is a lifetime maximum and occurred while the agent was baselining the 500-document corpus rather than during the attack - the arms wait 12 s after creating the corpus for exactly that reason, and A2's measured 1.972 s time-to-suspend bounds how far behind the agent can have been when it responded. No events were dropped in any arm. The honest split is therefore: about 1 s of it cannot be removed at all, and the rest is cost in the agent that has not been chased down. Cost per event is dominated by the per-path ledger read and the baseline write, not by detection, and neither has been optimised.
root_cause_of_the_remaining_failure.what_would_close_it: Only a mechanism that names the writer synchronously with the write - a filesystem minifilter, which is kernel-mode code requiring a signing certificate Microsoft issues to registered vendors. See docs/LIMITATIONS.md section 1. Widening any threshold here would change the reported number without changing the number of files the attacker actually got.

_what_this_does_not_show: That the agent stops ransomware. It shows that one of two third-party encryptor shapes is suspended mid-campaign with a measured time and a measured loss, that the other is missed for two separately documented reasons, and that three benign tools ran untouched in a configuration that was demonstrably capable of suspending something.
